chapter.v: Then Job responded:

“If my
grief could be weighed and my troubles placed on the scales

they would
be heavier than the sand of the sea. That's why I spoke so rashly.

For the
arrows of the Almighty are in me; their poison saps my spirit. God's terrors are lined up against me.

Don't wild
donkeys bray when their grass is gone? Don't cattle groan when they don't have food!

Can something
that's tasteless be eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the white of an egg?

I just
can't touch any food—even the thought makes me feel sick!

Oh, if
only I could have what I really want, that God would give me what I most desire—

that God
would be willing to crush me to death, that he would just let me die!

But it
still comforts me to know, making me happy through the never-ending pain, that I have never rejected the words of God.

Why should
I go on waiting when I don't have the strength? Why should I keep going when I don't know what is going to happen to me?

Am I
as strong as rock? Am I made out of bronze?

How can
I help myself now that any chance of success is ripped away from me?

Anyone who
isn't kind to a friend has given up respecting the Almighty.

My brothers
have acted as deceptively as a desert stream, rushing waters in the desert that vanish.

The stream
floods when it is full of dark ice and melting snow,

but in
the heat it dries up and disappears, vanishing from where it once was.

Camel caravans
turn aside to look for water, but don't find any and they die.

Caravans from
Tema looked, travelers from Sheba were confident,

but their
hopes were dashed—they came and found nothing.

Now you
are no help, just like that—you see my trouble and you're afraid.

Have I
asked you for anything? Have I told you to bribe anyone for me from your wealth?

Have I
asked you to rescue me from an enemy? Have I told you to save me from my oppressors?

Explain this
to me, and I'll be quiet. Show me where I'm wrong.

Honest words
are painful, but what do your arguments prove?

Are you
going to argue over what I said, when the words of someone in despair should be left to blow away in the wind?

You would
play dice to win an orphan; you would bargain away your friend!

Look me
in the eye and see if I'm lying to your face!

Don't talk
like this! Don't be unjust! What I'm saying is right.

I'm not
telling lies—don't you think I wouldn't know if I was wrong?”
